changes.detail: With AbsoluteJS beta.175, a route that throws is logged on the server whatever the request accepts, so React, Svelte, Vue and Angular projects and API calls log errors too, and the scaffolded HTML and HTMX error.html pages load their stylesheet in production. Angular pages keep their styles on hot updates under secureHeaders().
changes.summary: New projects use @absolutejs/absolute 0.20.0-beta.175

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS beta.172 type-checks Vue projects with vue-check, bundled with the framework, on Bun 1.4.4 and newer, and `absolute typecheck` always type-checks even when the project has its own `check` script. Beta.173 stops island pages and Vue lazy routes from exposing server file paths in production, streams React SuspenseSlot and StreamSlot content by default, keeps Angular `@defer` sections after hydration, and fixes dev serving of paths that contain spaces.
changes.summary: New projects use @absolutejs/absolute 0.20.0-beta.173

changes.detail: server.ts ended with its own `.onError(...)` after the routes. Registered there it never saw their errors, but since AbsoluteJS beta.171 any app `onError` stops the framework rendering `error.html`, so a throwing route answered a browser with a JSON 500 and nothing was logged. The handler also logged a full stack for every 404. server.ts no longer registers one, and HTML and HTMX projects get a `pages/error.html`. A route that throws on a page or HTMX request now renders it with status 500, AbsoluteJS logs the error on the server, and 404s log nothing. Outside development the page shows a generic message and no stack.
changes.summary: A route that throws on an HTML or HTMX page renders error.html, and the error is logged

changes.detail: `absolute typecheck` checks Vue with vue-check on Bun 1.4.4 and newer. vue-tsc stays in Vue projects because AbsoluteJS still supports Bun 1.4.2, where it is the checker, and `ABSOLUTE_TYPECHECK_CHECKER=tsc` uses it too. The project README says when it can be removed.
changes.summary: Vue projects keep vue-tsc only as the fallback for Bun older than 1.4.4

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS beta.171 stops production error pages from showing error text, stops serving /manifest.json, renders error.html when a route throws for HTML and HTMX pages, and fixes React islands, Vue routes and Angular base hrefs under `absolute start`. Backend HMR also keeps scoped state.
changes.summary: New projects use @absolutejs/absolute 0.20.0-beta.171

changes.detail: `--angular` and `--angular-dir` were silently ignored, so a non-interactive run never made an Angular project. They now work like the other framework flags. `--html --skip` without `--html-scripts` exited with "cannot prompt for --html-scripts"; `--skip` now defaults HTML scripts on, as the prompt does. `--no-html-scripts` still turns them off.
changes.summary: `--angular` and `--angular-dir` select Angular, and `--skip` no longer stops at the HTML scripts question

changes.detail: server.ts created `scopedState({ count: { value: 0 } })` inline in `.use([...])`. It is now `const visitorState = scopedState(...)`, passed as `visitorState`. Backend HMR keeps an unchanged top-level const, so visitors keep their counts when server.ts is edited, the form the AbsoluteJS backend HMR docs recommend.
changes.summary: The HTMX starter creates its scoped state as a top-level `const visitorState`

changes.detail: The Pages menu opened on hover through inline `onpointerenter` and `onpointerleave` attributes, which the strict CSP from `secureHeaders()` blocks: two violations on each page. The HTML page already handled hover in its script, so the attributes are gone. The HTMX page gets its own `scripts/htmx-example.ts` for it. An HTML page made with `--no-html-scripts` has no script, so its menu opens on click.
changes.summary: The HTML and HTMX starter pages run under `secureHeaders()` without CSP violations

changes.detail: The generated `typecheck` script ran plain `tsc --noEmit`, which skips .svelte and .vue files. It now runs `absolute typecheck`. Svelte projects get svelte-check alongside svelte2tsx, and Vue projects get vue-tsc, which `absolute typecheck` needs to check them. Vue projects also get vue-router 4 and Angular projects get @angular/router, for pages that export `routes`.
changes.summary: `absolute typecheck` passes out of the box for Svelte and Vue projects, and the typecheck script runs it
Full-stack SaaS (and any Absolute Auth project) starts before an OAuth app is registered

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS beta.170 fixes production security holes: page props, request context, island state and JSON-LD can no longer break out of their inline scripts, production servers no longer run development code paths or expose stacks on error pages, and the server bundle, SSR bundles and runtime manifests are no longer served as static files. Production servers also start from a read-only build directory, as in a non-root container, and stack traces point at the source. `absolute add` now edits the config this tool generates. Svelte HMR keeps component state, and Svelte pages that use context work under `absolute start`. New opt-in features include `secureHeaders()`, form actions, file routes, internationalization, self-hosted fonts, Web Vitals reporting, HTML includes and cross-framework navigation. The generated starters need no changes: their HTML and HTMX pages have distinct names, and they use no `{#await}` blocks or `pageRouterPlugin`, the two breaking changes and the one removal.
changes.summary: New projects use @absolutejs/absolute 0.20.0-beta.170, with its production security fixes
Full-stack SaaS projects start, and HTMX projects pass their own lint
The rate limiter no longer breaks a new project's type check

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS beta.168 type-checks Svelte page props in server files: `handleSveltePageRequest<typeof Page>({ props })` now fails on a missing, mistyped or unknown prop, as React pages do. Svelte projects install svelte2tsx, which `absolute typecheck` and `absolute dev` use to generate a declaration per component, and their tsconfig lists `.absolutejs/types/svelte` in `rootDirs` so tsc and editors resolve server imports to those declarations. Since beta.145 the framework also refreshes imported CSS and changed images during HMR, builds Svelte and Vue pages without the frameworks a project doesn't use, hydrates islands on HTML and HTMX pages with only `islands.registry`, stops the server `absolute start` started, and no longer imports absolute.config.ts at runtime in production.
changes.summary: New projects use @absolutejs/absolute 0.20.0-beta.168, and Svelte page props are type-checked

Starter typechecks exclude generated build, runtime, dependency, and distribution files, including a custom build directory, so running the development server does not add generated browser entrypoints to application checks. Angular compiler options and checks of actual application sources are preserved. Generated runtime sidecars are also ignored by Git.

New projects format with `absolute fmt` (Bun 1.4.4 `bun fmt`, Prettier-compatible) instead of installing Prettier; they pin @absolutejs/absolute 0.20.0-beta.145, and an older Bun skips formatting with a warning instead of failing the scaffold. React projects no longer install the deprecated eslint-plugin-react-compiler (its rules ship in eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7), whose zod-validation-error 3.x broke `absolute eslint` under Bun 1.4.4

changes.detail: New projects start on Elysia 2.0.0-rc.0 and the @elysia plugins' release candidates, with @absolutejs/absolute 0.20.0-beta.144, @absolutejs/auth 0.101.0 and @absolutejs/observability 0.7.0, which build against it. The generated server registers its error handler with `onError` (Elysia rc.0 renamed `error`). Version lookups for Elysia packages now follow npm's `rc` tag instead of fixed betas.
changes.summary: Scaffolds projects on Elysia 2.0.0-rc.0

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS beta.140: a dev page reconnects after a dropped connection without reloading, and keeps trying through long outages; edits to class and memo/forwardRef components show without a reload; production builds ship React's production build.
changes.summary: New projects use @absolutejs/absolute 0.20.0-beta.140: dev pages survive network drops

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS beta.139 makes Expo, React Native and the Expo code-signing tooling optional peers, so a new web project no longer installs them, nor node-forge and braces, which have high-severity advisories and no fixed release. `absolute mobile` installs them when a project adds an Expo app. beta.126 to beta.138 also bring the dead-stylesheet reload fix and `absolute typecheck` on `bun check`.
changes.summary: New projects use @absolutejs/absolute 0.20.0-beta.139: web projects no longer install Expo or React Native

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS beta.125 fixes Vue pages that reach a helper only through a re-export (`export { x } from "./y"`). Those helpers were never copied into the generated tree, so the page failed to build and answered 500 in dev.
changes.summary: New projects use @absolutejs/absolute 0.20.0-beta.125: Vue pages build through helper re-exports

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS beta.124 accepts `@absolutejs/auth` up to 0.96, so a project that adds a current auth no longer also gets auth 0.76.3 nested under AbsoluteJS. The duplicate had doubled the auth type declarations TypeScript loads. beta.124 also stops `/hmr-status` from counting closed or duplicate HMR clients.
changes.summary: New projects use @absolutejs/absolute 0.20.0-beta.124: one copy of @absolutejs/auth instead of two

New projects use @absolutejs/absolute 0.20.0-beta.123: React Fast Refresh works on a Bun with the reactFastRefresh fix (and `absolute dev` offers AbsoluteJS's patched Bun), edits keep applying after a React syntax error, and a React edit re-imports every changed module

Scaffold Prisma for every Prisma database (PostgreSQL, Neon, PlanetScale, CockroachDB, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, Turso, SQL Server on Prisma 7.10 driver adapters; MongoDB on Prisma 6.19.3) with a committed initial migration, typed handlers and prisma generate / db:migrate scripts
Accept --orm none as the help text documents, and refuse unsupported database, host and ORM combinations before writing any files

Scaffold Drizzle for every Drizzle 1.0 dialect (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, Turso/libSQL, SingleStore, SQL Server, CockroachDB) with a committed initial migration and db:generate / db:migrate scripts
Update registry dependency pins and generate compatible Elysia 2, Drizzle 1, Angular and HTMX starters with persistent auth, typed JSON subapps, and executable starter checks
Generate correctness-focused lint defaults with typed Drizzle checks and isolated Eden API subapps; consume eslint-plugin-absolute 0.12.0
Use the Elysia 2 error lifecycle verified against a fresh generated project
Generate the Elysia 2 onError lifecycle instead of an unsupported on error hook
